name: 13-quorum-sensing-coupling
title: Quorum-sensing coupling (proposed)
question: Does coupling through a single diffusible signal molecule synchronise the networked reactors as effectively as diffusing the internal proteins?
hypothesis: A dedicated autoinducer species produced and sensed per node, diffusing along the edges, provides indirect coupling sufficient for synchronisation at lower transport flux than direct protein diffusion.
objective: Extend the node SBML model with a signaling species and diffuse only that molecule; compare synchronisation to study 09.
description:
Proposed follow-up seeded from study 09. Replaces all-protein diffusion with biologically-realistic quorum-sensing coupling via one autoinducer.

(Baseline points at the composite this proposal would EXTEND; the new mechanism is not yet built.)

expected_behavior.name: qs-synchronises
expected_behavior.condition: signal-only coupling still collapses the across-node spread
expected_behavior.rationale: Indirect coupling through a shared diffusible signal is the canonical cell–cell synchronisation mechanism.

report.verdict_detail: Proposed follow-up — not yet built or run. Seeded from 09-sbml-nodes-coupled (quorum-sensing).
